I'll select a bounded structural probe rather than another control search, using the incumbent as the verified source.

**Actual feedback and its effect on my choice:** The latest candidate (holding weight .10, terminal .05) lost joint acceptance (F6, F23): holding position still passed (F74/F26) and terminal reach passed (F71), but holding speed failed (F48/F3), with holding_max_speed up by +0.00938 m/s (F7) and holding_max_error up by +8.09e-5 m (F54), while terminal error only marginally improved (−6.45e-5, F20). That is a trade-off, not an acceptance gain, so raising the holding weight is not a productive control lever; combined with the already dense control sampling across history (holding 0/0.05/0.1/0.3; terminal 0/0.05/0.1), further control search on those paths has low promise. By contrast, the structural domain is only represented at a single point (near .16 / far .11 / scale .95 / compliant), and that structure was the lever that achieved acceptance and cut mean update time. So the useful, affordable next evidence is a single-factor structural probe.
